newsitem.title: USA: New York's Sen D'Amato would lose to Ferraro--poll.
newsitem.headline: New York's Sen D'Amato would lose to Ferraro--poll.

text.p: New York State's Republican U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato would lose in a match-up with the former Democratic vice presidential candidate and Congresswoman Geraldine Ferraro, who has weighed making a bid, a poll said.

Nor was Ferraro the only candidate who would beat D'Amato: U.S. Housing Secretary Andrew Cuomo, son of former New York State Gov Mario Cuomo, would win by a margin of 48 percent to 36 percent, said the Quinnipiac College Poll.
The potential margin of victory for Ferraro, at 54 to 35 percent, was little changed from her showing in a March 5 poll by the Hamden, Connecticut-based survey group.

However, D'Amato would do better against two candidates who have said they plan to run, as New York City Public Advocate Mark Green has seen his 47 to 35 percent lead errode to a dead heat. And U.S. Rep. Charles Schumer, a Brooklyn Democrat, has lost ground since he said he would run against D'Amato and not Gov George Pataki, a race the Congressman now would lose by a 40 to 39 percent margin according to the poll.
"Geraldine Ferraro continues to dominate the field. But remember D'Amato usually polls low -- and always wins," said Maurice Carroll, director, Quinnipiac College Polling Institute.
D'Amato's approval rating, though still negative, edged up to 42 to 47 percent, which was an improvement over his 40 to 50 percent rating on March 5.
The survey of 917 New Yorkers who said they were registered voters was conducted from April 14 to 20, and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.2 percent.
